text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- The World Jewish Congress (WJC) met in Oslo to discuss the search for Jewish property stolen by the Nazis during World War II. Jewish leaders said WJC made plans for penetrating Swiss bank secrecy in search of unclaimed wealth of Holocaust victims.
- Prime Minister Torbjoern Jagland, speaking prior to budget talks in parliament, says the ruling Labour Party wants to cut private consumption by increasing taxes.
- Insurer Vital will have to reduce administrations costs by 120 million crowns by cutting up to 150 annual job equivalents. Vital is owned by Den Norske Bank (DnB).

- Norwegian state pension fund Folketrygdfondet sold four million A class shares in engineering and offshore group Aker ASA. The shares were sold at 143 crowns a piece. The total profit was 300 million crowns. Folketrygdfondet was the main opponent of the merger of Aker and fisheries-based investment group RGI.
- Oil company Saga Petroleum ASA is still in the competition to buy British Santa Fe Exploration.
